text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Defence Minister Volker Ruehe favours small-scale expansion of NATO before 1999.
- Decision on plans to raise postage costs postponed until December.
- Head of the Social Democrats in Thuringia says an east German politician could be SPD candidate for chancellor.
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl defends his government's decision to cut sick pay entitlements.
- Economics ministry says German economy is on course for growth.
HANDELSBLATT
- Kohl calls on trade unions to work together with employers and government to improve German competitiveness.
- Deutsche Bank plans to revamp branch structure.
- Deutsche Babcock AG restructuring to cost more than planned.
- Finance Ministry number two Juergen Stark calls for unanimity among EU members states to be maintained when it comes to tax matters.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Kohl warns employers not to break existing wage agreements.
- Search for kidnapped Frankfurt businessman Jakub Fiszmann continues without success.
- President Roman Herzog calls for Germans to embrace new media.
- Ecomomics ministry reports success in German exports but investment still stuttering.
- Mobile telephone operators plan price war for Christmas market.
DIE WELT
- Row reupts over state railway operator Deutsche Bahn's plans for new routes, which critics say overlap with those of the planned Transrapid high-speed railway.
- The IWH institute in Halle warns against applying west German wages to the east of the country.
- Federal government plans to invest 19 billion marks in local public transport by the year 2000.
